Ten products, Ads-IQ, Retention-IQ, Restock-IQ, Stores-IQ, Marketplaces-IQ, Crossborder-IQ, NPD-IQ, Concierge-IQ, Feeds-IQ and Partnership-IQ, share one set of numbers. They don't stop at recommendations: they make the changes too, at the level of control each brand chooses. It works inside Slack, plugs into 100+ tools from Shopify and NetSuite to Meta, Google and Amazon, and is running 23 brands today across paid media, retention, inventory and wholesale, stores, marketplaces, catalog and partnerships.

Every function has a tool. Nothing runs the whole. We built SuperchargeMe to run the whole.

The product is live and brands are paying for it. Getting it in front of the right brands is the next step. That's you.

The role in a sentence

Be our first marketer and own the go-to-market: fill the sales calendar with CEOs, CFOs, COOs, CMOs and VPs of E-Commerce at mid-market omnichannel brands, and grow the brands that sign up on their own.

Where we are

SuperchargeMe is already revenue-generating, with brands paying for it every month. What it doesn't have yet is a way for the next hundred brands to find it.

Who we sell to: mid-market omnichannel brands in the US, UK and EU, selling across their own store, marketplaces, wholesale and retail. Two ways in: brands starting with a single product sign up and get going on their own. Brands that want several platforms working together, with onboarding, book a demo.

There's no marketing team, agency or playbook yet. You start with a live website, a sales deck, a product you can demo, and case studies from our first clients that are being written now. A founding Account Executive starts alongside you, so every demo you book has a closer waiting, while sign-ups go straight into the product.

The story is ready to tell. Brands run ten to twenty tools, each now with its own AI, and none of them agree. We call it the Silo Tax. Naming it, and making brand leaders feel it, is the heart of this job.

The work

  • Set the go-to-market plan: which buyers and markets we go after first, and through which channels.
  • Run paid media yourself across Meta, Google, LinkedIn and anything else that works, alongside email, retargeting, campaigns aimed at named brands, events, and joint marketing with agencies, Shopify partners and systems integrators.
  • Work out which of our ten products to lead with for each type of buyer, and write the messaging for each.
  • Build and look after the route to a demo: landing pages, the booking flow, qualifying questions, quick follow-up and a clean handover to sales.
  • Grow self-serve sign-ups, from the first visit to an account that's actually using the product, including our Shopify App Store listing.
  • Turn our case studies and the founders' experience into posts, pages and short videos.
  • Use our own agents on your campaigns, starting with Ads-IQ on Google and Meta.
  • Report every week on demos, sign-ups, activation, pipeline and what each one cost.

What good looks like

We'll measure you on qualified demos and sign-ups, and the revenue they lead to.

Clicks, impressions and ROAS only matter as far as they get us there.

  • After your first month, tracking is set up properly, you've agreed the list of target brands with sales, and your first campaign is running.
  • After your first quarter, demos and sign-ups come in every week from channels you set up, and you know what each one costs by channel.
  • Sales starts asking for more of one kind of lead, because those are the deals that close.
  • The case studies already being written with our first clients are published, and sales uses them in every deal.

What you bring

  • At least four years in B2B demand generation or growth, ideally at a software company selling to e-commerce or retail brands.
  • You've run Meta, Google and LinkedIn campaigns yourself, including campaigns aimed at a list of named companies, without an agency doing it for you.
  • You can show the pipeline or sign-ups you've been responsible for, and what they cost.
  • You write well enough that a CMO reads to the end.
  • You build your own reporting in the CRM and analytics tools.
  • You already use AI tools and agents in your day-to-day work and can show us how. We sell AI agents, so we'd expect that.
  • You're comfortable being the first and only marketer for a while.

Bonus points

  • You've run a DTC or e-commerce brand.
  • You've built demand from zero at an early-stage B2B company.
  • You've run events or executive dinners in commerce or retail.

Skip this one if

  • Your best campaigns needed an agency to run them.
  • You report clicks and impressions and call it pipeline.
  • You'd rather write the plan than ship the campaign.
  • You want a remote or mostly remote role. We're together in North London Monday to Thursday.

Why join

  • You'll set up marketing from scratch, and you'll have a say in who joins the team after you.
  • Most brand leaders haven't yet seen AI that takes actions on their business. You'll shape how they first hear about it.
  • You'll work alongside both founders, who ran commerce brands before building software. Decisions are quick, and what you hear from the market gets into the product fast.
  • You can use our agents on your own work from your first day.

How we hire

  • A 30-minute intro call with the co-founders.
  • A short exercise: a one-page plan for getting qualified demos from mid-market omnichannel brands and growing sign-ups.
  • A working session with the founders on your plan.
  • References.

What you get

£60,000–£75,000 salary plus bonus

Share options so you own a real piece of what you build. Plus a company car and a strong benefits package.

In person in North London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays flexible

title: General Capabilities - Member of Technical Staff
descriptionHtml:
About Us

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous models and hardware. The General Capabilities team is developing the science that makes that possible: a principled, evidence-based method for building agentic systems automatically.

We are hiring for several positions on this team through one application. Depending on your background, you will work on our agent runtime, on evaluation, or on automated agentic system optimisation. We are looking for experienced systems engineers and researchers. Since we are an interdisciplinary team, we expect depth in one area and a willingness to work across the others.

What You'll Build

Depending on the position, you will work on some of the following:

  • Design and build stateful, asynchronous agent runtimes across distributed environments

  • Develop clear Python APIs, libraries, and DSLs with stable extension points for tools, backends, and new execution models.

  • Develop evaluation and observability tooling for long-horizon, tool-using agents.

  • Research methods that improve agents automatically, such as program search, routing, context management, multi-agent collaboration and post-training.

  • Work with our infrastructure teams to optimise agents for cost and latency on heterogeneous hardware.

What Sets You Apart

We are seeking candidates with demonstrable experience in one or more of these areas:

  • Experience building runtimes, workflow engines, distributed systems or developer frameworks that other engineers adopted.

  • Deep familiarity with the internals of SGLang, vLLM or comparable inference serving frameworks: scheduler design, memory management and execution pipelines.

  • Depth in multi-agent systems, program synthesis, or evolutionary and LLM-driven search over programs and agents, including systems that run the research loop themselves.

  • Experience with RL or post-training for long-horizon, multi-step or tool-use tasks.

  • Evaluations, benchmarks or agent harnesses you built that other people went on to use.

What We Offer

  • Equity & Ownership

  • Private healthcare

  • We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us

descriptionHtml:

title: Global Clinic Operations Lead
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

Neko is scaling fast. Our clinical teams already outnumber HQ across the US and Europe, and that ratio will keep growing. They deliver Neko’s promise to every member, every day – and right now, the information supporting their work is fragmented, inconsistent, and ungoverned. At our current pace, that's not just operational noise. It's a quality and safety risk. The role exists to fix that.

The role sits at the centre of two funnels. Inbound: you'll work closely with every team at Neko to shape what reaches clinical staff, when, and how. That means building trusted relationships across the organisation, helping teams understand what clinical staff need, and together making deliberate decisions about what gets communicated, what waits, and what can be consolidated. Outbound: once aligned and prioritised, you translate that into structured, cadenced formats that a dispersed clinical workforce can act on – right channel, right format, right frequency.

This is change management as much as communications. You're not just sending updates. You're redesigning how the whole organisation relates to its clinical teams.

 

What you'll deliver in the first 6-12 months

Build and enforce the intake model

  • Design the process that governs how every team at Neko communicates with clinical staff – how requests are submitted, evaluated, sequenced, and approved

  • Build the centralised view that ensures nothing reaches clinical staff in an uncoordinated or duplicative way

  • Document decision criteria clearly enough that stakeholders understand and trust how calls are made

  • Define escalation paths for urgent communications that need to move faster than the standard cadence

 

Drive organisation-wide change management

  • Partner with senior leadership to establish the intake model as an endorsed, org-wide norm – not an optional service, but the way Neko works

  • Run a structured roll-out across every team with touch points to clinical staff

  • Build the relationships that make the process feel collaborative rather than bureaucratic

  • Report regularly on intake volume, team compliance, and where we need to evolve.

 

Operationalise clinical communications

  • Start with a clear-eyed audit of how information reaches clinical teams today – the gaps, the overlaps, the friction

  • Build a global clinical programme with a single source of truth that clinical staff can rely on

  • Design the right mix of channels and formats for a dispersed, non-desk workforce – including AI-enabled formats like short-form video, audio briefings, and visual summaries

  • Create repeatable templates that make consistency straightforward for programme managers and local teams

  • Equip clinic leads with the tools and confidence to communicate well within their teams without losing global coherence

  • Define the metrics that prove it's working – comprehension, consistency, engagement, reduction in operational noise – and report on them regularly

  • Build a global communications cadence that helps leadership teams understand what’s changing, what’s ahead and how to prepare.

 

Minimum Qualifications

  • Proven experience in change management, or programme management, with direct ownership of communication or enablement strategy at scale

  • Proven experience designing and enforcing intake or governance processes across multiple cross-functional teams – you've built the model, sold it in, and made it stick

  • A track record running structured communications programmes for large, dispersed frontline workforces

  • Strong programme management instincts: you bring structure to ambiguity and build systems that hold

  • A creative communicator who knows when a policy document is right and when a 60-second video does the job better

  • Genuine fluency with AI tools and an appetite to use them to improve quality, efficiency, and reach

  • Sharp stakeholder skills: you can align leadership and cross-functional teams, hold the line when needed, and build trust in the process

  • Experience in high-growth, multi-site consumer services or healthcare strongly preferred

  • Comfortable working across multiple geographies and time zones

  • Strong written and verbal English; additional European languages a plus

About titles at Neko

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

title: Global Programmatic Architect
descriptionHtml:
At Jellyfish, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and inclusive collaboration. We welcome individuals who excel in collaborative, varied teams and value the unique contributions that each person brings to the table.

Jellyfish is a global digital marketing agency; a unique fusion of tech enthusiasts, creative minds, and media and data experts all united to empower our clients along their digital journey. Our commitment to embracing diverse perspectives fuels our innovation and strategies that challenge the status quo, reinvent media activation, and craft influential stories for our global clients and their customers. Join us in shaping a future where business growth and personal fulfilment go hand in hand.

Job Description

The Global Programmatic Lead (Programmatic Architect) is the senior technical practice leader for Programmatic Media across Jellyfish, sitting within the Domain Specialists hub and reporting to the Chief Solutions Officer - Media, Strategy & AI (CSO). You are the global custodian of how Jellyfish architects, engineers, automates, and commercialises programmatic activation across DSPs, SSPs, curation layers, bidding algorithms, and data clean rooms.

This is a senior role, there is no direct line management or people management but you are expected to collaborate with activation team leads & regional media leadership to affect positive change for Jellyfish clients. You are not running campaign ops or managing direct reports; you are the agency’s most senior programmatic technologist and systems architect. You define the global practice, codify frameworks for scaled delivery, contribute to our proprietary product roadmap, lead high-stakes pitches to win new business, drive technical advancement through strategic ad-tech partnerships, and serve as principal technical counsel to our highest-value global enterprise clients.

You partner closely with regional media and delivery leads across NA, EMEA, and APAC. While regional delivery teams execute programmatic campaigns in their local markets, you set the technical architecture, bidding methodologies, automation workflows, and delivery standards they operate from.

 

50% Product, Commercial & Technical Partnerships · 50% Client Strategic & Technical Leadership

The role is an intentional 50/50 split:

  • 50% Practice & Product Architecture: Designing buying & audience strategies, automation hooks/MCP integration, steering ad-tech integration roadmaps, managing top-tier tech partnerships (Google, The Trade Desk, Amazon, etc.), and spearheading major pitches.

  • 50% Client Strategic Leadership: Serving as principal programmatic strategist and trusted technical advisor for Tier-1 accounts, driving technical maturity (signal resilience, clean rooms, custom algorithms) and unlocking incremental retained revenue.

     

Your primary responsibilities will include:

 

1. Product Strategy, Automation & Technical Partnerships (50%)

  • Define the Global Programmatic Methodology: Own and update the global programmatic playbook, codifying standards across audience intelligence, bidding, algorithmic optimisation, curated marketplaces (PMPs/PG), dynamic creative optimisation (DCO), and identity/signal resilience.

  • Codify Delivery & Drive Automation: triage execution into fully automated, hybrid, or human-assisted workflows, handing off artefacts to delivery and MSP teams to streamline campaign build times and eliminate operational friction.

  • Contribute to Proprietary Product Evolution: Partner directly with Jellyfish Product teams to feed technical requirements, data schemas, and API automation hooks into internal tooling.

  • Ad-Tech Partnerships & Frontier Innovation: Own strategic technical relationships with core platforms (DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon, Google, premium SSPs, retail ad networks, clean rooms). Secure first-mover advantage on platform alphas and betas, testing them technically and translating them into deployable client solutions.

  • Product-Centric New Business: Architect winning product narratives, bespoke tech architectures, and commercial frameworks for major pitches and RFPs. Lead the programmatic discipline in tier-1 global pitches, driving high pitch-win rates and expanding retained scope.

  • Cross-Discipline Integration: Architect the connective programmatic layer across Search, Social, Retail Media, GEO, and Creative, building unified full-funnel activation frameworks (e.g., audience syncing, cross-channel frequency management, closed-loop attribution).

2. Client Strategic & Technical Leadership (50%)

  • Principal Technical Counsel for Tier-1 Clients: Act as the lead advisor for CMOs, Heads of Media, and MarTech executives at enterprise accounts - translating complex programmatic engineering into board-level growth strategies.

  • Drive Client Programmatic & AI Maturity: Actively advance Tier-1 clients along the programmatic maturity curve.

  • Brief Validation & Technical Governance: Serve as the technical filter on complex client briefs, ensuring brief feasibility and alignment with modern media architectures before execution.

  • Thought Leadership & External Voice: Represent Jellyfish as a category authority through POVs, white papers, analyst briefings, industry summits, and keynotes on topics like cookieless addressability, agentic media buying, and AI-driven curation.

     

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of advanced programmatic and ad-tech experience within an agency, DSP/SSP, ad-tech vendor, or sophisticated brand-side media team.

  • Expert Technical Proficiency across Enterprise DSPs: Deep technical fluency with platforms such as Display & Video 360 (DV360), The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, Campaign Manager 360, and major SSP curation tools.

  • Supply Path & Media Economics: Strong track record designing SPO frameworks, private marketplace (PMP) deal structures, and custom algorithm setups.

  • Track Record in Commercial Growth: Proven background contributing to high-value new business pitches, RFPs, and expanding programmatic scope in enterprise brand accounts.

  • No line-management required, but proven leadership through influence, upskilling, and technical mentorship across cross-functional teams.

Note: We emphasise skills, expertise and behavioural attributes over years of experience and traditional degrees. If you want to join our collaborative team, we invite you to apply today with your resume in English.

Additional Information

Join Jellyfish and experience a workplace where we prioritise your growth, celebrate your contributions, and empower you to tailor your work environment to suit your needs.

💰 Reward: You'll be eligible to join our discretionary annual bonus scheme.

💫 Custom Work Environment: Work remotely for up to 60% of your days and shape your day between 8am. and 6:30pm with flexible working hours.

👪 Family Support: Enjoy 14 weeks of paid leave for primary caregivers and 4 weeks of paid leave for secondary caregivers. We also provide £1000 (or equivalent) towards courses for returning primary caregivers to support your transition back into work.

title: Go-To-Market Associate
descriptionHtml:
Growth at Private Equity Insights

The world’s most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why Private Equity Insights

Private Equity Insights is the world’s largest Private Equity community with 1m PE professionals, delivering impact through 12 global PE conferences with thousands of the world’s best investors and operators such as Blackstone, BlackRock, Apollo, Carlyle, CVC, KKR, and many more.

Private Equity Insights is part of United Media (https://www.united-media.com/) which focuses on building large-scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, finance, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 5 media companies and exited 1.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

title: Graduate Sales Development Representative (London)
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Start your sales career at Pugpig, helping some of the world’s leading media brands to reach and engage their audiences. As a Graduate Sales Development Representative, you’ll be the first point of contact for prospective customers and help build a new-business pipeline across the UK, Europe and the Americas.

You’ll learn how to research target accounts, start relevant conversations , qualify opportunities and work with the sales and marketing teams to turn good prospects into meetings and future customers. This is an entry-level role with support, training and the opportunity to progress into a broader sales or account management role. The role is based at our Holborn office, with at least three days per week in the office.

Key responsibilities

  • Be the first point of contact for prospective Pugpig customers, starting relevant conversations and understanding their needs

  • Build new business pipeline across the UK, Europe and the Americas

  • Research and prioritise target account lists, identifying the publishers and contacts most likely to benefit from Pugpig

  • Run tailored outbound campaigns using cold calls, LinkedIn and email, adapting the message to each publisher and product

  • Generate and qualify sales opportunities, asking useful questions and deciding which prospects should move forward

  • Work alongside our Head of Marketing and the sales team to plan campaigns, share feedback and improve our approach

  • Respond to inbound sales queries promptly and helpfully

  • Support meetings, product demonstrations and industry events by researching prospects, preparing briefs, booking conversations and following up afterwards

  • Use HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator and AI prospecting tools to research accounts, run campaigns efficiently and keep learning about our customers

  • Maintain accurate and useful records in our CRM so that the wider sales team has a clear view of every opportunity

About Pugpig

  • We’re the best mobile publishing platform on the market and we work with the world's best media companies.

  • We work in close partnership with our customers to conceive, evolve, customise and operate our platforms, so they can focus on their core business.

  • Our platforms power hundreds of apps for the biggest media brands in the world, including The Independent, New Scientist, The Spectator, Condé Nast, Reach, DMG Media, Hearst and many more.

  • We work with news media, consumer magazines, B2B publishers and membership organisations.

  • Our teams in London and New York offer deep expertise and support to customers around the world.


About you

You’re at the start of your sales career, or have up to two years’ experience. You’re ambitious and excited to learn how tech sales works in media and publishing. You’re confident communicating with new people, curious about their businesses and able to explain ideas clearly. You are resilient, persistent and comfortable hearing “no” while continuing to follow up professionally.

You have a genuine interest in technology and can understand and explain simple technical concepts with clarity. You don’t need to have a technical degree, but you should be curious about how technology works and able to learn our products quickly. You'll become an expert in our products, services and sales process.

You’re super organised, detail-oriented and motivated by progress. You take coaching well, enjoy working towards shared goals and can manage your own activity. You’ll excel at researching leads and be great at starting new relationships. You're quick to learn and pick up new skills, and you'll be able to use your creativity to overcome challenges. You have an interest in media and publishing and can understand the requirements of the buyers and end-users of our products and services.

You’ll have these skills and qualities:

  • Positive, can-do attitude

  • Driven, keen to succeed and eager to learn

  • Excellent communicator (both verbal and written) and team player

  • Highly organised and uses initiative

  • Great eye for detail

  • Creative approach to problem solving

  • Good understanding of technology

Working at Pugpig

Here are some of the things you’ll experience if you come and join us:

  • You’ll be working with the world’s best media companies

  • Alongside an awesome, vibrant team of technology professionals

  • With a set of values that puts an emphasis on quality of life for all of our team members

  • We work hybrid in central London

  • Performance-related bonus scheme

  • Wellbeing support and healthcare options

  • Volunteering days every year so that you can support a charity that’s close to your heart

  • Training and conference budgets that help you stay on the top of your game

Our values

Be the solution

We take the initiative and seek to solve problems with creativity.

Make tomorrow better

We think critically about what will deliver our goals and improve tomorrow;

Our future selves will thank us.

Zoom out

We think big picture and look beyond our immediate field of vision.

Be kind

We communicate with kindness, openness and respect;

We approach interactions with a positive and supportive attitude.

Enjoy the ride

We have fun and prioritise quality of life, even when we’re up against it.

If this role sounds like a great fit, get in touch with us, we’d love to hear from you!

Pugpig is committed to promoting an inclusive culture. We believe that diversity leads to a happier and more productive working environment.

We welcome suitably qualified applicants from all different backgrounds.

Please let us know if you have additional requirements. We are happy to make the necessary accommodations so that we can facilitate a positive recruitment process.

title: Graphic Designer (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
🛠️ Wir sind Gauder. Wir machen DIY-Produkte besser.

🌍 Seit 2017 haben über 3 Millionen Kundinnen und Kunden in Europa und den USA bei uns bestellt. Heute sind es mehr als 100.000 Bestellungen im Monat.

🎨 Ob im Geschäft oder auf Amazon: Der erste visuelle Eindruck entscheidet in Sekunden, wer zugreift und wer weitergeht. Darum ist Design bei uns kein Nebenthema, sondern ein wichtiger Hebel für unseren Erfolg.

🤝 Gemeinsam mit unserem Head of Design gestaltest du, wie unsere Kundinnen und Kunden Gauder erleben: auf der Verpackung, im Amazon-Listing und in jeder Präsentation. Dein Bereich gehört dir. Du kannst Dinge direkt verändern, siehst unmittelbar, was sie bewirken, und legst Wert auf die Details, an denen andere sparen.

Beginn: ab sofort

Anstellung: Vollzeit, unbefristet

Ort: Berlin (Mitte)

Aufgaben

  • Verpackungen: Du gestaltest Verpackungen für neue und bestehende Produkte, vom ersten Entwurf bis zur druckfertigen Datei.

  • Listings: Du erstellst Produktbilder, Infografiken und A+ Content für unsere Amazon-Listings in ganz Europa.

  • Präsentationen: Du gibst unseren Präsentationen die Form, mit der sie sich von der Masse austauschbarer Decks abheben: klar, prägnant und unverwechselbar.

  • Designsystem: Du denkst in visuellen Systemen statt in Einzelstücken und siehst unsere Marken nicht als fertiges Regelwerk, sondern als etwas, das mit dem Unternehmen wächst. Du entwickelst die Designsprache laufend weiter und hinterfragst bestehende Lösungen, auch deine eigenen.

Qualifikation

  • Ausbildung: Du hast Grafik- oder Kommunikationsdesign studiert (Universität, FH, Kolleg) oder eine Ausbildung gemacht. Dein Können und dein Portfolio sind uns wichtiger als dein Abschluss.

  • Erfahrung: Du hast 1–3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Grafikdesign, idealerweise mit Print-Projekten oder im E-Commerce.

  • Tools: Du arbeitest routiniert mit der Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop etc.) und Figma.

  • Sprachen: Du sprichst Deutsch und Englisch mindestens auf C1-Niveau.

  • Auge fürs Detail: Dir fallen fehlende Millimeter und verschobene Pixel auf, bevor sie teuer werden.

  • Haltung: Du hast Geschmack und kannst ihn begründen. Du gehst offen an Dinge heran, recherchierst, probierst aus und stellst Fragen. Wenn es noch keine Antwort gibt, zerlegst du das Problem, um eine Lösung zu finden.

Pluspunkte

  • Foto & Video: Du kannst Produkte selbst in Szene setzen, als Studio- und Lifestyle-Foto oder als kurzes Produktvideo.

  • 3D: Du hast Erfahrung mit 3D-Modelling und Rendering (Cinema 4D/Blender).

  • E-Commerce: Du hast bereits für Amazon oder andere Online-Marktplätze gestaltet.

Benefits

  • Design mit Reichweite: Was du gestaltest, landet jeden Tag tausendfach bei unseren Kundinnen und Kunden, auf Produkten, die in ihrer Kategorie gegen die ganz Großen bestehen.

  • Kurze Wege: Du arbeitest an unseren eigenen Marken, ohne Agentur-Umwege, endlose Meetings oder Review-Schleifen. Wir treffen Entscheidungen direkt im Team.

  • Urlaub: 28 Urlaubstage.

  • Arbeitsumfeld: Flexible Arbeitszeiten, Home-Office und ein Büro in zentraler Lage in Berlin, mit Kaffee, Getränken und Snacks.

  • Ausstattung: Aktuelle High-Performance Hardware

Klingt nach dir?

Dann schick uns deinen Lebenslauf, ein kurzer Überblick reicht völlig. Viel mehr interessiert uns, was du kannst:

  1. Dein Portfolio (Link oder PDF), gerne mit Verpackungs- oder E-Commerce-Arbeiten.

  2. Ein Projekt, bei dem dein Design etwas bewirkt hat, mit ein paar Sätzen dazu: Welches Problem hast du gelöst, und was hat sich verändert (z. B. Klickrate, Verkauf, Verständlichkeit)? Bei Teamprojekten: dein Anteil.

Lange Bewerbungsprozesse sparen wir uns. Passt dein Profil, hörst du innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns, und im ersten Gespräch sitzt du gleich mit unserem Head of Design zusammen.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!

Dort finden Frauen mit ihren Kindern zeitweise Unterschlupf und Schutz vor Gewalt und werden von weiblichen Fachkräften psychosozial betreut.

Das Diakonische Werk sucht für unser Frauen- und Kinderschutzhaus ab dem 01.01.2027

eine Hausmeisterin

Die Stelle ist zunächst auf 2 Jahre befristet, mit der Aussicht auf Entfristung. Der Arbeitsumfang umfasst 12,5% (4,9 Wochenstunden). Die Vergütung erfolgt nach TVöD/KAO (EG 5).

Aufgaben

Sie unterstützen die Mitarbeiterinnen und Bewohnerinnen mit ihren Kindern dort, wo handwerkliches Geschick gefragt ist und kümmern sich um Haus und Garten. Zu ihren Aufgaben gehören neben dem Rasenmähen und Baumschnitt im Garten auch allerlei kleine Reparaturen im und um das Haus herum. Sollten Fachfirmen involviert sein, koordinieren Sie deren Einsatz in Absprache mit der Hausleitung.

Qualifikation

Neben handwerklichen Geschick und einer "Ärmel-hoch"-Mentalität ist gerade für die Tätigkeit im äußerst sensiblen Umfeld eines Frauen- und Kinderschutzhauses Verschwiegenheit und Fingerspitzengefühl gefragt. Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Absprachen mit den Angestellten setzen wir voraus. Ein gültiger Führerschein ist Grundvoraussetzung für die Einstellung.

Eine handwerkliche Ausbildung ist natürlich wünschenswert, gerne sind wir aber auch bereit geeigneten Quereinsteigerinnen eine Chance zu geben.

  • Eine interessante, abwechslungsreiche und sinnvolle Tätigkeit in einem geschütztem Umfeld

title: Head of Data Protection (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
At Quantum Systems, we develop advanced autonomous systems for defence and security across multiple domains, combining unmanned platforms with integrated software and AI.

As Head of Data Protection, you will play a key role in building and strengthening Quantum Systems’ Group-wide Data Protection Management System (DPMS). You will develop the Group privacy framework and coordinate its implementation and continuous improvement across our international entities, translating legal and technical requirements into pragmatic processes and controls.

This is a leadership role with responsibility for developing the Group privacy framework and coordinating its implementation across the Group. As part of the integrated Governance, Risk & Compliance organization, you will work across corporate functions, entity management, business process owners, external Data Protection Officers (DPOs) and local privacy coordinators. Entity management and business process owners retain their respective responsibilities for compliance and operational implementation. DPOs retain their independent advisory and monitoring functions.

What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Develop and continuously enhance the Group privacy framework, translating GDPR and international privacy requirements into clear governance, responsibilities, processes and standards, and coordinate implementation with local entities.

  • Coordinate the Group-wide implementation and continuous improvement of the DPMS, consolidating privacy risks, remediation actions and implementation evidence and tracking outstanding measures with the responsible owners.

  • Support business functions in establishing practical privacy processes, including data subject rights and incident response, and assess technical and organizational measures, IT architectures, cloud services and international data flows in collaboration with IT and Information Security.

  • Coordinate external DPOs and local privacy coordinators, working closely with entity management, business process owners, GRC, Legal, HR, IT and Information Security, and support engagement with regulators and auditors within the relevant responsibilities.

  • Report material privacy risks, outstanding actions and implementation progress to Group management, providing clear, decision-relevant information while preserving management accountability and the independent advisory and monitoring functions of DPOs.


What you bring to the team:

  • Several years of relevant experience in data protection or privacy management, with proven experience establishing and implementing privacy management systems in international organizations.

  • Strong legal expertise in GDPR and international privacy requirements; qualification as a lawyer and a recognized Data Protection Officer certification are highly desirable.

  • Strong technical privacy competence, including the ability to assess technical and organizational measures, IT architectures, cloud services and international data flows in collaboration with IT and Information Security.

  • Strong analytical and implementation capabilities, with a proven ability to translate complex legal and technical requirements into pragmatic, scalable processes, effective controls and documented implementation evidence.

  • Strong project and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to coordinate cross-functional stakeholders without direct reporting lines and communicate clearly with business functions and senior management.

Why Quantum-Systems:

  • We believe in the power of combined efforts: straightforward tech expertise paired with a customer-centric focus.

  • We are industry pioneers who are ambitious, bold, and visionary.

  • We push limits, think outside-the-box and strive for technological excellence to shape the future of aerial data.

  • We promise to be your runway for individual and professional growth.

Our benefits:

  • Company pension scheme: We support you so that you can already make provisions for later.

  • Flexible working hours: With trust-based working hours, you are not only responsible for your working hours, but also for your work-life balance.

  • Mobile Work: If things get a little busy in the office, you have the option to work remotely one flexible day per week to create the right balance.

  • Stay active: With EGYM Wellpass, you get access to thousands of fitness and sports facilities — and of course, we subsidize the membership.

  • Bike-Leasing: We support you in staying environmentally mobile and healthy.

  • Corporate Benefits: Your opportunity for attractive offers and discounts from well-known suppliers and brands, e.g. Adidas, Apple, Expedia.

  • Employee events: We not only want to grow together, but also celebrate our successes together.

  • Lunch-Card: Be powerful with delicious energy, daily lunch budget is sponsored.

  • Company Shuttle: Enjoy our convenient shuttle service that picks you up from Laim in Munich and brings you to our location, with return trips at the end of the workday.

About us:

Quantum Systems is a leading European deep-tech company for unmanned systems across air, land and maritime domains. We develop, produce and scale integrated hardware, software and AI-powered solutions designed for mission-critical operations in complex environments.

Our systems combine autonomous platforms, advanced sensors, secure communications, mission software and AI to deliver actionable information, enable faster decision-making and support operations across domains – from the air to the ground and at sea.

Headquartered in Gilching near Munich, with locations across Europe and worldwide, Quantum Systems develops its core technologies in-house. This integrated approach enables us to rapidly innovate, scale and deliver mission-ready solutions while strengthening European technological sovereignty.

Quantum Systems operates in the global dual-use market, serving armed forces, security organizations, public institutions, and industrial and infrastructure customers. Our systems support a broad range of missions, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), situational awareness, critical infrastructure protection and complex multi-domain operations.

What sets us apart is the combination of hardware, software and AI within one integrated ecosystem - built to connect systems, data and operators across domains.

Our mission is clear: Accelerate the world’s transition to unmanned systems for a better future.

Our commitment:

We are an open-minded company that not only values diversity, but actively promotes it. Regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation or disability, we firmly believe that the diversity of our employees is an essential part of our success.

At our company, every voice is heard and every perspective is valued. We believe that our differences enrich us and help us to find creative solutions and generate innovative ideas. We pride ourselves on creating an inclusive work environment where all employees can reach their full potential.

title: Head of Exchange Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.


We're looking for a Head of Exchange Infrastructure to own the layer every Kraken product is built on: the matching engine, core infrastructure, third-party custody, the algo engine and the API engine. Kraken grew up as a set of vertically integrated products, each with its own engine and its own APIs. This role consolidates them into a single exchange stack that serves every product and every interface. You will lead a team of four to five product managers, partnered with an engineering manager. It is a senior, independent team, which means you get leverage quickly and you are expected to stay close to the work.

 

The opportunity

  • Own the product vision and roadmap for the exchange layer: matching engine, core infrastructure, third-party custody, algo engine and API engine

  • Lead and grow a team of four to five product managers, and set the bar for product craft across the layer

  • Lead the consolidation of multiple matching engines into one, starting with US derivatives, then international derivatives, then spot

  • Build interface-agnostic, so every product team and every interface can build on the same platform rather than their own

  • Define success metrics (p99 latency, throughput, uptime, resiliency) and hold teams accountable to them

  • Partner with engineering leaders across exchange and core infrastructure to sequence the migration without disrupting live markets

  • Partner with Risk and Credit Infrastructure so a client can hold one account and trade every product against it

  • Anticipate industry shifts and shape our platform to stay ahead

  • Align cross-functional teams (product, engineering, risk, compliance) around the exchange strategy

 

What you bring

  • Senior product leader with experience in exchange, trading, or high-performance platforms

  • Experience managing and developing product managers, on a team senior enough to run without you in the room

  • Happy to be a player-coach. This team is independent, so you will own roadmaps and write specs yourself at times, not only review them

  • Proven ability to set product vision and translate it into a long-term roadmap

  • Strong understanding of matching engine and market data architecture, and the tradeoffs low latency forces

  • Experience building platforms for internal customers, with the judgment to tell a platform from a series of bespoke builds

  • Excellent communication skills — can influence technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • A passion for crypto markets, market structure, and building the next generation of infrastructure

 

Nice to haves

  • Engineering background before moving into product, so you've built or operated high-performance systems yourself and not just specced them

  • Experience across both spot and derivatives venues, with the market structure differences that come with each

  • Time at a crypto exchange operating at comparable scale, volume and uptime expectations

  • Track record building platform roadmaps that interlock with adjacent product orgs rather than running in isolation

   

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

Your job is to build, lead and scale LemFi’s business across Asia, driving sustainable growth, strong country-level ownership and regional profitability.

As Head of Asia, you will own the regional strategy and commercial performance across China, the Philippines, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and any new markets launched across the region. You will lead and develop Country Managers, empowering them to own their country-level P&Ls while maintaining accountability for the region’s overall financial performance, growth and profitability.

You will translate LemFi’s broader business objectives into clear regional priorities, ensuring every market has a focused growth strategy, disciplined budget management and measurable commercial targets. You will oversee annual strategic planning, quarterly growth priorities and monthly execution plans, ensuring that country teams remain on track to deliver their targets and adapt quickly when performance or market conditions change.

You’ll combine strategic leadership with hands-on commercial execution. One day, you might be reviewing regional P&L performance and reallocating budgets across markets; the next, coaching a Country Manager on acquisition strategy, evaluating a new market opportunity, negotiating a strategic partnership or addressing a market that is falling behind its growth targets.

You will establish a high-performance operating cadence across the region, using data and commercial insight to identify opportunities, address underperformance, share best practices and allocate resources where they can generate the greatest impact. You will work closely with product, marketing, operations, compliance and finance to ensure that regional plans are supported by the right capabilities and executed effectively.

You own the regional numbers, the performance of your markets and the development of your leaders. Your mission is to make Asia a major engine of sustainable growth and profitability for LemFi.

What you'll build and own

  • Regional P&L and commercial performance. Own the overall Asia regional P&L, with accountability for revenue, transfer volume, gross profit, acquisition costs, retention, operating expenditure and profitability. Translate regional objectives into market-level targets, monitor financial performance and take decisive action to close gaps and improve returns.

  • Country leadership and accountability. Manage, coach and develop Country Managers across China, the Philippines, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and future markets. Set clear expectations, establish performance standards and ensure each Country Manager has the direction, resources and accountability needed to deliver sustainable growth.

  • Country-level P&L ownership. Empower and enable Country Managers to run their own country P&Ls, make informed commercial decisions and take ownership of their market's financial outcomes. Build their capabilities in budgeting, forecasting, unit economics, channel investment and profitability, while maintaining appropriate regional oversight and alignment.

  • Regional growth strategy and planning. Own the regional growth strategy and oversee the development and execution of annual business plans, quarterly growth plans and monthly operating plans across all markets. Ensure plans are grounded in market opportunity, clear performance targets, realistic budgets and measurable initiatives. Review progress regularly and adjust priorities as needed.

  • Performance management and operating cadence. Establish a consistent rhythm of business reviews across the region, including monthly performance reviews, quarterly planning and regular growth and budget calibration sessions. Track performance against targets, identify risks and opportunities early, and ensure every market has clear actions to address underperformance.

  • Budget allocation and resource optimisation. Oversee regional marketing and growth budgets, ensuring investment is allocated to markets and channels with the strongest potential returns. Identify forecast underspend, evaluate opportunities to accelerate growth and reallocate resources where appropriate to maximise regional impact and new-user acquisition.

  • Market expansion and new-country launches. Identify and evaluate opportunities to expand into new Asian markets. Develop market-entry strategies, assess commercial potential, define investment requirements and coordinate launch plans across product, marketing, operations, compliance and finance. Establish clear launch milestones and ensure new markets have the leadership, infrastructure and commercial plans needed to scale.

  • Customer acquisition and marketing effectiveness. Supervise country-level acquisition strategies across paid and organic channels, partnerships, referrals, community networks and other distribution opportunities. Ensure teams optimise against measurable outcomes, including new users, customer acquisition cost, conversion, transfer volume, retention and lifetime value. Encourage experimentation and the adoption of successful approaches across markets.

  • Strategic partnerships and distribution. Guide Country Managers in identifying, negotiating and developing strategic partnerships that accelerate acquisition and transaction growth. Support high-value regional partnerships where relevant, establish effective commercial frameworks and ensure partnerships translate into measurable business results.

  • Pricing, unit economics and profitability. Oversee market-level pricing strategies and unit economics, ensuring each country balances competitive customer propositions with sustainable margins. Challenge investment decisions, review corridor and channel profitability, and help teams identify opportunities to improve contribution and long-term commercial performance.

  • Market intelligence and competitive strategy. Maintain a strong understanding of customer behaviours, diaspora communities, competitive dynamics, regulatory considerations and market-specific opportunities across Asia. Translate market insights into regional priorities and ensure Country Managers adapt their strategies to local customer needs.

  • Cross-functional leadership. Partner with product, marketing, finance, operations, compliance and other central teams to align regional priorities with company-wide objectives. Represent the needs of Asian markets in central planning and ensure teams have the capabilities, resources and support required to execute their growth plans.

  • Leadership development and organisational effectiveness. Build a strong regional leadership team by developing Country Managers into commercially capable, accountable business owners. Establish clear decision-making frameworks, encourage collaboration and knowledge sharing across markets, and foster a culture of ownership, urgency and continuous improvement.

  • Executive reporting and strategic decision-making. Provide clear, data-led updates on regional performance, financial forecasts, growth opportunities, key risks and resource requirements. Present recommendations to senior leadership and drive decisions that support LemFi's long-term growth and profitability.

Your experience

  • An experienced regional commercial leader: 10–15 years of experience across fintech, payments, remittances, financial services or high-growth businesses, with a track record of managing substantial commercial targets and preferably multi-market P&L responsibility.

  • A proven people leader: Experience managing senior market leaders, Country Managers or commercial teams across multiple geographies. You know how to set direction, coach leaders, build accountability and create high-performing teams.

  • Strong P&L ownership: Demonstrated experience managing revenue, costs, budgets, forecasts and profitability. You can connect country-level commercial decisions to overall regional financial performance.

  • A strategic growth operator: Experience developing and overseeing annual strategies, quarterly plans and monthly execution priorities. You can translate business objectives into clear plans, measurable targets and consistent delivery.

  • Commercially and analytically sharp: Strong understanding of customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, conversion, gross profit, retention, unit economics and channel performance. You use data to challenge assumptions, identify opportunities and make resource-allocation decisions.

  • Experienced in market expansion: A track record of launching, scaling or entering new markets, assessing commercial potential and coordinating cross-functional execution in complex environments.

  • Strong budget and investment management: Experience overseeing multi-market budgets, identifying performance gaps, reallocating investment and balancing growth ambitions with financial discipline.

  • A partnership and distribution builder: Experience developing strategic commercial relationships, negotiating agreements and building acquisition channels that deliver measurable growth.

  • Hands-on and execution-focused: Comfortable moving between regional strategy, financial reviews, leadership coaching and operational problem-solving. You act decisively, take ownership and thrive in a fast-moving environment.

  • A strong cross-functional collaborator: Able to align product, marketing, finance, operations, compliance and other teams around shared priorities while balancing regional requirements with company-wide objectives.

  • Adaptable across diverse markets: Comfortable operating across different customer segments, cultures, competitive environments and levels of market maturity. Experience across Asian markets or diaspora-focused businesses is an advantage.

  • An accountable and empowering leader: You establish high standards while giving capable teams the autonomy to make decisions. You know when to coach, when to challenge and when to intervene to protect business performance.

Nice to have

  • Remittance and payments experience: Experience scaling international money transfers, cross-border payments or digital wallets, with a strong understanding of FX pricing, corridor economics and customer behaviour.

  • Experience across Asian markets: Existing knowledge of one or more of China, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh or the Philippines, including relevant customer segments, competitive dynamics and commercial opportunities.

  • Multi-country P&L experience: Previous responsibility for a regional business spanning multiple markets, with a demonstrated ability to balance local market ownership and regional financial objectives.

  • Market launch experience: Experience taking new markets from initial opportunity assessment through launch and into sustainable growth.

  • Diaspora and distribution networks: Relationships with relevant community organisations, student associations, employers, influencers and other distribution partners across key sending and receiving markets.


Why join LemFi?

Your work here puts money back into families' pockets. That's the reward, and the weight of it. You'll take on some of the hardest problems in finance alongside people who do their best work when the stakes are real. We move fast and we expect a lot, because our customers can't afford for us to do otherwise. In return you get room to own real problems, global impact you can see, and a team that won't slow you down.

Bring grit and ownership and there's a place for them here. Ambition belongs here, come and show us yours.

Follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store or Google Play.


Don't feel that you're right for this role, but want to submit your interest in working for LemFi? You can join our talent community to stay in touch for future opportunities.

Recruitment agencies notice

LemFi does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruitment agencies. We work only with agencies on our preferred supplier list, and only when we’ve asked them for their support. Any CVs sent to us outside this arrangement will not incur a fee.

AI in hiring at LemFi

We use AI to cut admin, like notetakers that let interviewers focus on the conversation instead of typing. AI never makes hiring decisions. That responsibility always sits with our hiring teams. Read our AI use policy to see how we use AI and how we expect you to use it too.

title: Head of Internal Control, Operational Risk - CDI (F/H)
descriptionHtml:
Lemonway est un établissement de paiement européen agréé, qui accompagne les marketplaces et les plateformes de crowdfunding dans plus de 29 pays.

Nous fournissons des services de paiement sécurisés, conformes et évolutifs pour la nouvelle économie, notamment des services de KYC, de traitement des paiements, de détection de la fraude, de ségrégation des fonds et de gestion des comptes. Notre expertise technologique et réglementaire permet à nos clients de développer leur activité tout en respectant les standards les plus exigeants en matière de conformité et de sécurité.

Avec plus de 150 collaborateurs, Lemonway est une entreprise dynamique et internationale, au cœur de l’économie numérique. Nous combinons l’agilité d’une scale-up avec les exigences et les responsabilités d’un établissement financier réglementé.


Le poste

Rattaché(e) a notre Chief Compliance & Risk Officer, vous prenez en charge les activités de contrôle interne, de gestion des risques opérationnels et de gouvernance de Lemonway.

Vous veillez à ce que le profil de risque de l’entreprise soit correctement identifié, évalué, suivi et communiqué, tout en contribuant au renforcement de son environnement de contrôle et de sa culture du risque.

Vous managez une équipe de deux personnes et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec le CEO, la Direction générale, les fonctions de contrôle et les équipes opérationnelles. En tant que véritable business partner, vous accompagnez l’entreprise dans ses prises de décision, tout en vous assurant que ses activités restent conformes aux exigences réglementaires applicables, aux politiques internes et à l’appétit au risque défini.

Il s’agit d’un poste stratégique et opérationnel, particulièrement adapté à une personne qui apprécie de construire et d’améliorer des dispositifs dans un environnement international, en forte évolution et réglementé.

Puisqu’il s’agit d’un poste centré sur la deuxième ligne de défense, nous recherchons des expériences en risques opérationnel et contrôle permanent au sein d’un établissement de paiement réglementé. Ce poste ne relève pas du contrôle financier, du FP&A, de la comptabilité, du contrôle de gestion ou du reporting financier.

Les principales responsabilités :

Contrôle interne et contrôle permanent

  • Piloter et améliorer en continu le dispositif de contrôle interne de niveaux 1 et 2.

  • Définir, maintenir et mettre en œuvre le plan annuel de contrôle permanent.

  • Veiller à ce que les contrôles soient correctement conçus, documentés, réalisés et justifiés.

  • Développer les indicateurs de contrôle pertinents et les reportings destinés à la Direction et aux instances de gouvernance.

  • Identifier les faiblesses du dispositif de contrôle, évaluer leur impact et coordonner les actions correctives.

  • Promouvoir une culture forte du contrôle et de la gestion des risques dans l’ensemble de l’organisation.

  • Contribuer à la mise en place et à l’optimisation des outils et processus de type GRC.

Risques opérationnels et gestion des risques

  • Piloter le dispositif de gestion des risques opérationnels, notamment l’identification, l’évaluation et le suivi des risques.

  • Coordonner la préparation et la mise à jour régulière des cartographies des risques de l’entreprise.

  • Organiser et maintenir le Risk Appetite Framework, ainsi que le suivi des indicateurs d’appétit au risque.

  • Piloter le processus de gestion et de reporting des incidents, en veillant à ce que les incidents soient enregistrés, analysés et suivis de manière appropriée.

  • Suivre les risques opérationnels, non financiers et émergents, notamment les risques liés à la technologie, à la cybersécurité, à la fraude, à l’externalisation et aux processus métiers.

  • Préparer des reportings risques clairs et exploitables à destination de la Direction générale et des instances de gouvernance concernées.

Gouvernance et comités

  • Préparer, coordonner et animer le Comité des risques trimestriel.

  • Accompagner le Chief Compliance & Risk Officer et la Direction générale dans leurs prises de décision liées aux risques.

  • Préparer les supports de gouvernance, tableaux de bord et présentations offrant une vision claire de l’environnement de risques et de contrôle de l’entreprise.

  • Coordonner la définition et la mise à jour des rôles et responsabilités, notamment au travers des matrices RACI.

  • Contribuer aux processus de reporting réglementaire et interne, notamment au rapport annuel sur le contrôle interne, ainsi qu’aux autres reportings réglementaires applicables.

Audits et contrôles réglementaires

  • Coordonner les audits externes, réglementaires et internes portant sur le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels et la gouvernance.

  • Être le point de contact principal des auditeurs et des autorités compétentes sur les sujets de contrôle interne.

  • Gérer les demandes d’audit, la collecte des éléments justificatifs, le suivi des constats et les actions associées.

  • Coordonner la préparation et la mise en œuvre des plans d’actions correctifs et préventifs.

  • Suivre l’avancement des plans de remédiation et présenter les actions à risque élevé ou en retard aux instances de gouvernance appropriées.

  • Coordonner le programme de contrôle périodique et suivre sa mise en œuvre conformément au plan d’audit défini.

Externalisation, continuité d’activité et résilience opérationnelle

  • Garantir la robustesse et la bonne exécution du dispositif PSEE.

  • Contribuer au pilotage des activités externalisées et des prestataires tiers, conformément aux exigences réglementaires applicables.

  • Piloter les activités de continuité d’activité et de résilience opérationnelle de l’entreprise.

  • Maintenir et tester régulièrement les plans de continuité d’activité.

  • Participer aux exercices et aux réunions de gestion de crise lorsque cela est nécessaire.

  • Identifier les opportunités permettant de renforcer la résilience de Lemonway et sa capacité à maintenir ses activités critiques en cas de perturbation.

Politiques, procédures et formation

  • Évaluer les besoins de création ou de mise à jour des politiques, procédures, formulaires et documents de contrôle.

  • Coordonner la rédaction, la revue et la mise en œuvre des procédures de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques.

  • Concevoir ou contribuer à la création de supports de formation et de sensibilisation.

  • Veiller à ce que la documentation soit claire, opérationnelle, à jour et alignée avec le modèle de fonctionnement de l’entreprise.


Expérience

  • Vous disposez d’au moins 8 ans d’expérience dans le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels, l’ERM, l’audit, la conformité ou un domaine proche.

  • Vous avez évolué dans un environnement réglementé, idéalement dans le secteur du paiement ou en fintech.

  • Vous avez déjà encadré une équipe et travaillé sur la structuration ou la transformation d’un dispositif de gestion des risques et de contrôle interne.

Compétences recherchées

  • Solide connaissance des dispositifs de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques opérationnels.

  • Bonne compréhension de l’environnement réglementaire français et européen, notamment des attentes de l’ACPR, des orientations de l’EBA, des exigences LCB-FT et de la DSP2.

  • Expérience du fonctionnement d’instances de gouvernance et de la préparation de reportings destinés à la Direction générale.

  • Maîtrise des environnements de transformation, de croissance ou de scale-up.

  • Expérience de la mise en place ou de l’évolution d’outils GRC.

  • Très bon niveau de français et d’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.

  • La connaissance de l’allemand ou d’une autre langue européenne constitue un atout.

Qualités personnelles

  • Leadership affirmé et bonnes compétences managériales.

  • Esprit structuré, rigoureux et grande capacité d’organisation.

  • Autonomie, tout en appréciant le travail collaboratif.

  • Approche pragmatique, orientée solutions et résultats.

  • Solides capacités d’analyse et grande attention aux détails.

  • Excellentes compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes.

  • Capacité à challenger de manière constructive et à convaincre des interlocuteurs de tous niveaux.



Avantages

  • Bureaux au cœur du Sentier (Paris 2e)

  • Poste hybride (2j TT / semaine, et 3 semaines de full-remote par an)

  • Carte Swile

  • Mutuelle Alan

  • Prise en charge à 50% du pass Navigo/Vélib

  • Accès à Gymlib

  • Prime vacances Syntec & RTT

Lemonway s'engage à promouvoir la diversité, notamment en favorisant le mixité Femme/Homme et l'emploi de personne en situation de handicap.

title: Head of Legal @ AI Chip DeepTech Venture, Dresden / Berlin
descriptionHtml:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.


About the Venture

We build brain-inspired computing hardware designed to tackle problems that conventional computing handles badly or not at all. Our technology has its roots in leading European research and is now a commercial system, being deployed by research institutions, supercomputing centres and companies internationally.

We are a deep-tech company moving from research-led development into a much larger commercial operation. We are scaling our hardware deployments, expanding our international customer base and building the organisation and infrastructure to support the next phase of growth.

We recently closed fresh funding, are around 70 employees in size and based out of our Dresden HQ.

About the Role

This is our first legal hire.

Legal currently sits largely with the managing directors. Your mandate is to build the legal function, establish clear decision rights and create the infrastructure that allows the company to scale without unnecessary friction.

You will own legal end to end, from corporate and commercial through to export control, IP and product regulation. The remit is broad because we sell sophisticated, regulated hardware internationally and are moving faster than our processes have historically allowed.

This is a role for someone who enjoys both the legal and operational sides of the job: not simply answering questions, but building the frameworks, processes and decision-making structures that prevent the same questions from coming up repeatedly.

What you'll do

  • Own corporate governance across our German GmbH and US entity: shareholder and board matters, financing rounds, related-party and conflict-of-interest questions.

  • Lead commercial contracting across hardware sales, licensing, research collaborations, cloud and service agreements, and NDAs. Build the templates and playbook so that standard cases can be handled efficiently.

  • Take ownership of export control and dual-use matters, including EU Dual-Use Regulation, German licensing requirements, US export-control exposure, sanctions and restricted-party screening.

  • Lead our cybersecurity and product compliance agenda, including NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act and related incident-reporting and conformity requirements.

  • Cover product safety and market access for the hardware itself, including CE marking, EMC, RoHS, REACH and product liability.

  • Manage our IP portfolio: patents, freedom to operate, trade secrets, licensing, technology rights and trademarks.

  • Manage compliance obligations connected to public funding, including grant conditions, record keeping and audit readiness.

  • Work with People & Culture on employment matters, including contracts, terminations, employee participation structures, immigration. Data protection and GDPR sit here too.

  • Oversee open-source licence compliance and software supply-chain obligations together with engineering.

  • Build the delegation layer: signing authority, approval thresholds, decision rights and clear ownership, so that routine hiring, procurement and commercial decisions do not automatically converge on the managing directors.

  • Decide what we keep in house and what goes to external counsel, then manage those firms and the associated budget.

About You

You are comfortable being the only lawyer in the building, and you see that as an opportunity rather than a risk. You enjoy the operational side of legal work as much as the technical side.

You are direct, commercially minded and comfortable making judgement calls. You know where your own limits are and are happy to bring in specialists when the question warrants it.

  • Qualified German lawyer (Volljurist), with fluency in EU regulation.

  • In-house experience at a semiconductor, hardware or deep-tech company, ideally in a start-up or scale-up environment rather than exclusively in a large corporate legal department is strongly preferred.

  • Experience with export control and dual-use questions in a business that actually ships internationally, including an understanding of the difference between licensing and per-transaction screening.

  • Comfortable across a wide surface: corporate, commercial, IP, employment and regulatory. You do not need to be the deepest expert in each area, but you need to know what good looks like and when to escalate.

  • You have built structure inside a company before: templates, approval frameworks, signing authority or something equivalent that outlived your involvement.

  • Familiarity with hardware product regulation, CE marking, RoHS and REACH, or with the evolving EU cybersecurity regime is a strong plus.

  • German and English at working fluency, both written and spoken.

  • Based in or willing to relocate to the company's location in either Dresden or Berlin.

Why Join

You would be shaping the legal function of a company with direct access to the managing directors.

The subject matter is unusually interesting: brain-inspired computing, advanced hardware, international technology sales, export-controlled technology, research partnerships and a regulatory environment that is evolving in real time.

The work environment is flexible and inclusive, and we offer a competitive salary with relocation support for the right person. If you want to build something meaningful rather than maintain something that already exists, this is that kind of role.
